summary: Fan out rule-observer agents over game traces, dedupe by ruleId, adversarially verify each unique finding.

confirmed.violation: Rule 460 states that a Combat occurs when a Cleanup occurs, there are no items on the Chain, there is a staged Combat at a Battlefield, and no Showdown or Combat is ongoing elsewhere — i.e. combat initiation is mandatory at Cleanup, with the turn player's only choice being WHICH battlefield (461.1). The engine instead surfaces `startShowdown` as an elective move and permits the turn player to take other actions (exhaustRune, activateAbility) while combat is staged, chain is empty, and no showdown is ongoing.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts:809 (startShowdown implemented as elective; comment miscites "Rule 548: Discretionary Action"); packages/riftbound-engine/src/cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:296 (Cleanup step 6 lacks rule 323.12/323.13 forced showdown/combat initiation); packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/turn.ts:67 (only gate is on endTurn, not on other discretionary actions)
confirmed.notes:
Rule text supports the claim. Rule 460 + 323.13 (Cleanup step 10): "If the current state is a Neutral Open State and one or more Combats are Staged at Battlefields, the Turn Player chooses one of those Battlefields. Combat begins there." Rule 319.8 makes Cleanup an outstanding task after every Move; rule 344 likewise says a Showdown "begins…during a Cleanup" — initiation is mandatory, the only choice is which battlefield.

Engine: `startShowdown` (chain-moves.ts:809-881) is defined as an elective enumerated move gated only on `neutral-open` + `bf.contested`; the Cleanup implementation (state-based-checks.ts:296-331) never initiates combat/showdown — it only returns a `combatPending` list. Nothing in riftbound-flow.ts forces the move. `endTurn` (turn.ts:67-71) is the sole gate — it merely blocks ending the turn while a bf is contested, so `exhaustRune` (resources.ts:67, no timing gate at all), `recycleRune`, `activateAbility` (chain-moves.ts:423) and `playGear` remain enumerated alongside `startShowdown`.

Trace (do_not_commit/wf-traces/game-r2-7.jsonl — the claim's "game-wf-7.jsonl" filename is slightly off): seq=42 post-state has bf1.contested=True, showdownStack=[], no chain; available=[concede, exhaustRune×2, recycleRune×2, startShowdown] → chose exhaustRune; seq=43 chose exhaustRune again; startShowdown not taken until seq=44. seq=123 has bf2.contested=True, showdownStack=[]; available=[concede, recycleRune×2, activateAbility(legend), startShowdown] → chose activateAbility; seq=124 then even offers playGear before startShowdown is finally chosen. All match the claim.

Minor inaccuracies in the claim: the "which-battlefield" choice is rule 323.13 (not 461.1 as cited), and `contestedBy` is None in the trace so "combat staged per 461" is inferred from opposing-unit presence rather than an explicit staged flag — but neither affects the verdict. The seq=123 activateAbility case is the least defensible for the engine (legend activated ability is unambiguously a Discretionary Action that should not fit between Move-completion and mandatory Combat initiation).

confirmed.violation: Rule 319.8 requires a Cleanup after a Move completes; Cleanup step 10 (323.13) states that if the turn is in a Neutral Open State and one or more Combats are Staged, the Turn Player chooses a Battlefield and Combat begins there. Per 320.1, Priority is not awarded while a Cleanup is in progress, so no other Discretionary Actions may be taken before the staged Combat opens. The engine instead returns full Neutral-Open Priority to the Turn Player and offers `startShowdown` as an optional discretionary move alongside playGear/playSpell/activateAbility/exhaustRune/recycleRune, letting the Turn Player defer the staged Combat and take arbitrary Neutral-Open actions first.

The engine only flips contested=true when the destination already has an opposing unit present (seq 65/112/188), but the null-controller empty case is skipped even though 450 (and 190.3.a) require it.
